Despite its renowned reputation in Milan and the excellent reviews I've read, I can only warn future clients.
I understand this is a long comment, but I strongly recommend reading it to get a complete picture of what you can expect at this practice.
I brought my dog ​​in for a septic cataract, the result of a penetrating scratch from a cat.
He began treatment with eye drops on February 3rd.
On February 7th of this year, at the second visit, he began antibiotic treatment with Vibravet (I was reprimanded because the treatment plan actually called for it from day one, while I had understood that it should be administered after the pre-operative blood tests).
The dog is in excellent health, lively, and has a good appetite, as can also be seen from the report from the visit he had on February 5th at another center, Oncopets, for a breast nodule, which was described as benign and not noteworthy.
On February 13th, around 12:00 p.m., he performed blood tests. Pre-operative
Despite the fact that the results, already available to the doctors at 1:21 PM that same day, reported life-threatening liver values ​​(ALP 247, ALT even OFF THE SCALE!!!), NO ACTION was taken and I was not warned in any way... on the contrary...
On February 17, I called the office because the dog was sick, vomiting, and had no appetite.
I was ordered to ABSOLUTELY NOT stop taking the antibiotic and was sent a prescription for a gastroprotective drug (sucralfin).
FINALLY, on the afternoon of Saturday, February 22nd, I received a phone call informing me that the dog had severe liver failure.
During the past 9 days, the dog had taken Vibravet, which was also indicated in the package insert to increase the ALT and ALP liver values.
Who warned me about the problem, he initially takes care to tell me "He's not taking antibiotics, right?" And when I answered no, she reassured me with, "It can't be that anyway. He definitely has a problem, perhaps a tumor. He needs an ultrasound... but you should ask his vet, we don't want to interfere."
When asked, "Why did you take 10 days to let me know?" I first received an admission, "There was a bit of a mix-up," then a "We've just received the follow-up tests from a second clinic."
The same argument would be supported by the head doctor, Dr. Baracchetti, the following Monday.
The tests from the second clinic showed an ALT of 3780.
That afternoon, no help was offered, not even a simple IV.
The following Monday, the values ​​were obviously even higher, around 4500. At any point during these 10 days, the dog could have died.
After a week of hospitalization at the Anicura clinic, 4 different ultrasounds, various histological samples from the spleen and liver, tests for leptospirosis and various liver diseases. All results were negative, and the values ​​returned to normal.
The most likely conclusion is that the drug, although normally well tolerated, caused my dog ​​to develop hepatitis.
But even if, by some absurd chance, the hepatitis was due to external factors, it's foolish not to have reported it.
She is now well, but she has lost sight in that eye and will likely need enucleation.
It's pointless to describe the anger and the financial and emotional damage she has suffered in recent months.
I have detailed evidence of the incident described here.
I am working to file a report of the facts cited here with the relevant authorities, but before then, I made sure to notify all users.
Simone Altana
Optimal
